source_record.problem: Small-scale experiments can change the fresh-versus-repeated data regime and thereby select a recipe that transfers poorly.
source_record.insight: Preserve each source's repetition count while scaling tokens per active parameter; distinguish forecast validation from retrospective equal-loss efficiency fitting.
source_record.method: Source-scaled ladders; joint LR/weight-decay search; intermediate-scale prescription checks; separate BPB-versus-FLOPs and wall-clock comparisons.
source_record.result: Reported MAI-Base-2 ladder forecast and a separate retrospective FLOPs-efficiency interpolation. Proposed narrative emphasizes the protocol, not a universal speedup.
source_record.limitation: Internal evaluation data and simultaneous recipe changes; no independent reproduction. Figure 3 includes completed MAI-Base-2 in fitting. BPB/FLOPs does not establish generation quality or elapsed-time advantage.
source_record.sections_read: Official HTML technical sections from model comparison through scaling data; PDF pp.1–6 text including architecture table and Figures 2–4 labels/captions. No PDF pixel inspection, code audit, or full experiment rerun.
source_record.changes_existing_conclusion: Deepens T1 recipe/extrapolation conditions and links to T2 repetition; does not overturn Kaplan/Chinchilla or establish universal hyperparameter coefficients.
source_record.evidence_status: Newly discovered locally in the overlapping window, not published this calendar week. Website publication date printed 2026-10-15; no revision timeline disclosed.

decisions.placement: T1 after §6 Llama 3 and before §7, short subsection on preserving the training regime in scaling ladders. Link to T2 repetition and T3 cost accounting without duplicating their full discussions.
decisions.proposal_en:
Scaling ladders must preserve the regime whose behavior they predict. Microsoft AI’s 15 October 2026 report restricts each source’s unique examples in smaller runs so that its repetition count matches the final run, while keeping tokens per active parameter fixed. This source scaling addresses a recipe-transfer failure: small runs seeing fresher data may favor insufficient regularization for the larger repeated-data run. The report also jointly tunes learning rate and weight decay, then validates fitted prescriptions at an intermediate scale.

Evidence types remain separate. Figure 2 reports a ladder extrapolation to MAI-Base-2, whereas the advertised equal-loss FLOPs advantage uses another fit that includes the completed model and interpolates its matching point. It is not an independently validated prediction of that advantage, a wall-clock speedup, or a capability-wide ranking. Internal bits-per-byte evaluations and a jointly changed data, optimizer and architecture recipe also limit causal attribution. This adds a practical check to budget forecasting: reproduce data reuse and optimization conditions in the small-scale experiments, then distinguish forecast validation from retrospective efficiency estimation.
decisions.proposal_zh:
缩尺实验必须保留它要预测的训练状态。Microsoft AI 于 2026 年 10 月 15 日发布的报告，在保持每个活跃参数对应 token 数不变时，限制小规模训练中各数据源的唯一样本，使其重复次数与最终运行一致。这种 source scaling 针对一种配方迁移失败：小实验看到较多新数据，可能选择不足以应对大规模重复训练的正则化。报告还联合调节学习率和权重衰减，并在中间尺度验证拟合配方。

这些证据需要分开：图 2 报告向 MAI-Base-2 的阶梯外推；宣传中的等损失 FLOPs 优势则来自另一个包含已完成模型的拟合，其匹配点属于插值。它不是这一优势的独立预测验证、墙钟加速或全能力排名。内部 bits-per-byte 评估，以及数据、优化器和架构同时变化，也限制了因果归因。由此，预算预测多了一项实践检查：让小实验复现数据重用与优化条件，并区分前瞻预测验证和事后效率估计。

checks.facts: Fixed training tokens per active parameter; source repetition counts preserved by subsampling unique examples. Figure 2 labels L18–L42 as fitting ladder and final MAI-Base-2 as extrapolation/predicted-versus-actual.

Four separate internal held-out BPB evaluations; 4.2–12.3x versus DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Base is fitted equal-loss FLOPs comparison including completed MAI-Base-2. No matching training job at each inferred point or wall-clock ratio established.

Grid in log LR and log(LR×WD); weighted quadratic surfaces estimate minima; empirical prescriptions checked at an intermediate scale. HTML and plotted coefficient rounding differs slightly, so proposal omits coefficient precision.

80B active / 2.8T total; 50T tokens; 16k GB200 for38 days. Reported overall MFU21% uses2.5PFLOPS BF16 denominator and excludes rematerialization/optimizer; goodput89% is time fraction, not MFU. Layer MFU24→35% is a different measurement.

Every-layer MoE previously lost on time despite FLOPs benefits; grouping and multi-round dropless capacity control changed the practical optimum. More capacity means more memory; less can require extra rounds. Not evidence that sparse routing has zero systems overhead.

limitations: Figure2 prediction protocol is reported, not independently preregistered or reproduced here.
Reported BPB and the use of some post-trained external checkpoints do not justify capability-wide ranking.
PDF query parameter v=2 is not treated as a dated second publication.

source_record.title: Scaling Multilingual Mixture-of-Experts: How Language Coverage Changes Capacity and Compute Allocation
source_record.problem: Separate multilingual and MoE laws do not show whether added experts offset language-coverage costs or how preservation targets alter allocation.
source_record.insight: Jointly model active/stored capacity, experts, per-language exposure, coverage and diminishing repetition returns; evaluate shared languages under explicit resource constraints.
source_record.method: 64-configuration Top-1 grid, structured configuration holdouts, selected seed and mixture controls, larger-model stress test; separate logical and measured hardware accounting.
source_record.result: At matched target-language exposure, the common-language coverage penalty falls83% from dense to32 experts. Selected law mean holdout RMSE0.03319 versus refitted JointMoE(D_t)0.04617; not unseen-language generalization.
source_record.limitation: Fixed corpus/tokenizer/Top-1 recipe; primary grid one seed. Reused endpoints are correlated; formula selection uses validation comparisons; no independent final-test or replication established. Hardware and downstream-task benefits do not follow uniformly.
source_record.sections_read: v3 abstract and §§1–8; Appendix A setup/seeds/optimizer, B.1 fitting, B.2 selected ablation text/tables, B.3 parameterization, B.4–5 diagnostics/larger-model evaluation, C.1 and C.6 controls, D mixture controls, E allocation, F.1 protocol plus F.3 summary, G diagnostics, H physical cost. Large external benchmark tables and all figures not exhaustively audited; no code or experiment rerun.
source_record.changes_existing_conclusion: Adds coverage and per-language preservation as allocation axes in T3; deepens existing effective-data and cost boundaries rather than asserting every MoE scales better.
source_record.evidence_status: First release10/14; v2 10/15; v3 10/21. Current v3 read; complete v1-v3 semantic diff not performed.

decisions.placement: T3 §1 after the existing joint MoE configuration discussion (and optionally after sparsity/hyperparameter subsection), before DeepSeekMoE landmark. Cross-link T2 mixture and repetition without duplicating its full model.
decisions.proposal_en:
Expert capacity must be allocated against the diversity it serves. Dag et al. (v3, 21 October 2026) jointly model active parameters, expert count, language coverage and repetition-adjusted exposure. Their main grid contains 64 Top-1 configurations with 93M–590M active parameters. Across the same twelve languages, expanding coverage from twelve to two hundred produces a smaller mean loss penalty with 32 experts than with a dense model: the reported reduction is 83%, at matched active parameters and target-language exposure. Total tokens are not held equal in that comparison.

The fitted law is tested on held-out configurations, but each evaluated language already has fitted coefficients; this is not prediction for unseen languages. Larger-model and longer-horizon extrapolation remains conditional, and restoring average quality can leave individual languages worse off. Nor does logical compute establish physical cost: the authors report a median 1.69-fold GPU-hour increase for 32 experts versus dense models in matched configurations. Main-grid seed coverage is limited, and downstream accuracy interactions vary by task. The result makes coverage a resource-allocation variable without establishing universal expert benefits.

专家容量必须结合它服务的数据多样性来分配。Dag 等的 2026 年 10 月 21 日 v3 联合建模活跃参数、专家数、语言覆盖和扣除重复收益后的数据暴露量。主网格包括 64 个 Top-1 配置，活跃参数为 93M–590M。对共同的十二种语言，在匹配活跃参数和目标语言训练量后，把覆盖从十二种扩展到两百种，32 专家模型的平均损失惩罚比稠密模型小；报告降幅为 83%。这一比较并未保持总 token 数相同。

拟合规律在留出配置上测试，但所有评估语言已经有拟合系数，不能解释为对未见语言的预测。更大模型与更长训练的外推仍有条件；恢复平均质量也可能让个别语言变差。逻辑算力同样不代表实际成本：作者在匹配配置中报告，32 专家相对稠密模型的 GPU 小时中位倍率为 1.69。主网格的种子覆盖有限，下游准确率的交互效应也随任务而变。结果把语言覆盖纳入资源分配，却不能建立专家容量普遍有益的结论。
